title: Layer-Readout Interfaces in EEG Foundation Models: Predictive Accessibility and Cross-Dataset Transfer
abstract: arXiv:2611.31320v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Intermediate layers often outperform final layers when foundation models are used as frozen feature extractors, but the source of this advantage is unclear. We study this question in EEG foundation models by separating three factors: how representations are read out, whether intermediate layers provide predictive utility beyond the final-layer interface, and whether useful depth structure transfers across datasets. Across five models and three tasks, improving the final-layer readout consistently recovers substantial predictive performance, yet intermediate layers remain advantageous within frozen extraction. We also find that layers selected on one dataset remain useful on another across five dataset pairs and four task families, and that a compact set of source-derived task directions retains predictive value after transfer in sleep staging. Together, these results show that predictive utility varies across depth, and its usefulness

translated_title: EEG基础模型中的层读出接口：预测可及性与跨数据集迁移
translated_abstract: 当基础模型被用作冻结特征提取器时，中间层的表现往往优于最终层，但这一优势的来源尚不清楚。我们在EEG基础模型中通过分离三个因素来研究这一问题：表征如何被读出、中间层是否在最终层接口之外提供额外的预测效用，以及有用的深度结构是否能够跨数据集迁移。在五个模型和三个任务的实验中，改进最终层读出始终能够恢复相当可观的预测性能，然而在冻结提取方式下中间层仍保持优势。我们还发现，在一个数据集上选出的层在其他数据集上依然有用（验证跨越五个数据集对和四个任务族），并且一组紧凑的、源自源数据集的任务方向在迁移到睡眠分期任务后仍保留预测价值。综合来看，这些结果表明预测效用在网络深度上存在变化，其有用性
tldr: 本研究解析了EEG基础模型中间层优于最终层的原因：改进最终层读出接口即可恢复大部分预测性能，但冻结提取下中间层仍具优势，且所选择的层与任务方向能够跨数据集迁移。
en_tdlr: This study disentangles why intermediate layers outperform final layers in frozen EEG foundation models, showing that improved final-layer readout recovers much of the predictive performance, yet intermediate layers remain advantageous under frozen extraction, and that selected layers and task directions transfer across datasets.
